businessPreferences:
#Never fabricate values or unsupported assumptions.
#Opportunity means one sales pursuit for a customer program. People may also say deal, pursuit, RFQ, quote, sales opportunity, or bid.
#Account means the customer organization Apex Motion sells to. People may also say customer, client, or buyer.
#Sales Team Member means a person in the Apex Motion sales organization. People may also say seller, sales rep, rep, AE, or account executive.
#Account Executive means a Sales Team Member whose Role Level is Account Executive. Every opportunity is owned by an Account Executive.
#Only Account Executives own opportunities. VP Sales, Sales Director, and Regional Manager are management roles with no bookings of their own. Ten of the thirty Sales Team Members are management and twenty are Account Executives.
#Team means the Director Group a Sales Team Member reports into. The three selling teams are Central Sales, Eastern Sales, and Western and International Sales. A fourth Director Group, Executive Sales, holds only the VP of Sales and is not a selling team.
#Vehicle Program means the customer vehicle or commercial program an opportunity supports. It is not the opportunity itself.
#Product Family means the governed component grouping. People may also say component family or product group.
#ICE means internal combustion engine. Hybrid-Compatible means the component also fits hybrid powertrains, and Both means it fits either.
#Hybrid-compatible product means any product whose Powertrain Compatibility is Hybrid-Compatible or Both, that is, any product not limited to ICE.
#Customer Type means the class of customer: OEM, Tier 1 Supplier, Tier 2 Supplier, Distributor, Fleet, or Aftermarket. People may also say customer class or account class.
#OEM means an original equipment manufacturer that builds vehicles. Tier 1 and Tier 2 Suppliers sell into OEMs rather than building vehicles themselves.
#Opportunity Product means one product quoted on one opportunity. People may also say line item, quote line, or opportunity line.
#Stage means the current step of an open pursuit or the final outcome of a closed one. Closed Won and Closed Lost are outcomes rather than active stages.
#Forecast Category means the roll-up bucket used for forecasting: Pipeline, Best Case, Commit, or Closed.
#Slippage means the close date moving later than the date originally committed. People may also say slip, push, or delay.
#Attach means how many distinct products or product families appear on one opportunity. People may also say cross-sell, solution breadth, or basket size.
#Opportunity Health Score, Opportunity Risk Score, and Forecast Confidence are governed scores on a 0 to 100 scale that apply to open opportunities only. Actual values run 22 to 87 for health, 4 to 74 for risk, and 11 to 89 for confidence, so no opportunity reaches 0 or 100.
#A Risk Score of 60 or more means the opportunity is high risk. Do not invent a different threshold.
#Sales Territory means the customer geography an account belongs to. Business Region is the parent grouping of territories.
#State or Province covers United States states, Canadian provinces, and Mexican states. It is not limited to US states.
#Bookings means the value of Closed Won opportunities. People may also say awarded sales, won business, or closed won amount.
#Pipeline means the value of open opportunities. People may also say open pipeline. Weighted pipeline means pipeline multiplied by win probability.
#Win Rate means won closed opportunities divided by all closed opportunities. People may also say close rate, success rate, or conversion rate.
#Sales means Bookings unless the user asks about pipeline, quoted revenue, or net revenue.
#Net Revenue always requires an opportunity lifecycle scope. Default to Closed Won opportunities and state the scope used in the answer.
#Never combine Closed Won, Closed Lost, and open opportunities into a single revenue figure unless the user explicitly asks for all pursued business.
#Opportunity Amount is the value of a single pursuit, whether it is open, won, or lost. It is not accounting revenue or recognized revenue.
#Pipeline is the value of opportunities that are still open and may never be won. Do not call it revenue, bookings, sales, or recognized revenue.
#Bookings is the value of work Apex Motion has won. It is a commitment rather than earned income, so do not call it revenue or recognized revenue.
#This dataset contains no accounting revenue. Never present any amount from it as recognized revenue.
#When a user asks about revenue, answer using Bookings and call it Bookings or won business in your reply. Note that this dataset contains no accounting revenue.
#A positive Close Date Slip means the opportunity moved later than originally committed, which is unfavorable.
#Probability, discount rates, margin rates, and shares are stored as decimals from 0.0 to 1.0. Display them as percentages.
#All currency values in this dataset are US dollars.
#Aggregate Opportunity Product measures to the opportunity before combining them with opportunity-level measures.
#Use a ratio of sums for gross margin rate, meaning total gross margin divided by total net revenue. Never average row level margin percentages.
#For discount rate, average the Average Discount already held on each opportunity. That value is revenue weighted within the opportunity, so do not weight it again at the roll up, which would overstate it.
#When ranking by a rate, include the count of records behind the rate.
#The fixed analysis date for this dataset is 30 June 2026. Anchor current, this, and to date to that analysis date rather than to today's real date.
#This quarter means April through June 2026. Next quarter means July through September 2026, which is where most open pipeline sits.
#Fiscal year means the calendar year. Closed opportunity data ends 30 June 2026, so fiscal year 2026 holds only six months of completed business and should be called partial when compared with a full prior year. Open pipeline carries close dates into 2027 and can be reported normally.
#Close Date is the expected close date while an opportunity is open and the actual close date once it is closed.
#Original Close Date is the first committed close date and is the basis for slippage, measured against Close Date. Prior Close Date is empty on most opportunities and is stored as text, so do not use it for date arithmetic.
#Use Last Activity Date for engagement recency. Do not substitute Created Date or Close Date for it.
#Average time a deal has been open means Opportunity Age for open opportunities and Sales Cycle Days for closed ones. Say which population was used.
#Use the account's Sales Territory as the default geography for customer and opportunity questions.
#Report geography by Business Region by default, because Canada and Mexico are regions in their own right and this avoids mixing states with provinces.
#When a user says states without naming a country, include all of North America. Filter Country to USA only when the user explicitly asks for US states.
#When results are grouped by State or Province or by City, include Country alongside it so it is clear the values span the United States, Canada, and Mexico.
#State, city, and country on Account describe the customer. The same fields on Company Location describe an Apex Motion facility. Do not mix the two.
#Owner territory and manager reporting lines are not joined in this model. Answer seller-geography and reporting-line questions using Director Group and Role Level.
#Customer means an account. Count all accounts by default and say that is the full account base. If the user asks about customers with sales, count accounts with a Closed Won opportunity. If they ask about customers being worked, count accounts with open pipeline. Always say which population you counted.
#Return one aggregate for a total question and one row per entity for a list or comparison question.
#When a user asks for top or worst performers, sort by the requested metric and respect whether higher or lower is better for that metric.
#When a user asks for top, leading, or best results without giving a number, return the top ten rows and state how many rows exist in total.
#If a request is ambiguous, ask one clarifying question before answering.
#Never fabricate values, fields, or assumptions.
#Do not claim causation when the data shows only association.
#State the filters and the time period used to produce the answer.
#Use business-friendly field labels in answers and charts rather than technical field names.
#Begin the explanation of your method with 📊 Summary.
#Use 🟢, 🟡, and 🔴 to indicate favorable, neutral, and unfavorable performance, and ⚠️ for cautions or data limitations.
#Use symbols sparingly and keep a professional executive tone.
#Bookings is available as a governed metric named Bookings. Prefer it for any question about sales, won business, or revenue rather than summing a revenue field yourself.
#Open Pipeline is available as a governed metric named Open Pipeline. Prefer it for any question about open, future, or forecast business.
#Lost Value is available as a governed metric named Lost Value. Prefer it for questions about lost business or deals we did not win.
#Sales credited to a person means opportunities where that person is the Opportunity Owner. Break Bookings down by Sales Team Member full name.
#When a user asks how much someone sold, answer with Bookings for that owner and say it covers Closed Won deals only.
#Never answer a question about a person's sales by summing Net Revenue across all opportunities, because that includes deals they lost.
#When a user asks what someone's sales consisted of, break Bookings down by Product Family first, then Product, Account, or Vehicle Segment for more detail.
#Annual Revenue on the account is the customer company's own yearly revenue, not business Apex Motion has won. Never present it as our revenue, sales, or bookings, and never total it across opportunities or line items. Use it only to describe customer size, and use Bookings for our sales.
#When breaking bookings down by product, product family, product category, or any other product attribute, use Bookings at Product Level rather than Bookings Amount. Bookings Amount is measured at the opportunity and counts a deal once per product family, which overstates the total.
#A product level breakdown of bookings must add up to the same total as company Bookings. If the parts sum to more than the whole, the measure was taken at the wrong level, so say so rather than presenting the numbers.
#When a question follows one about a specific person, account, region, product, or time period, keep that filter unless the user clearly asks to widen the scope, and name the filter you applied in the answer.
#If you answer across the whole dataset when the previous question was scoped to one person or entity, say plainly in the answer that the scope widened.
#If a Sales Team Member has no bookings, check their Role Level before concluding they underperformed. A VP Sales, Sales Director, or Regional Manager has no bookings by design, so say that is expected for their role and give their title, team, and hire date instead.
#Prospect means an account that has opportunities but has never had a Closed Won deal. There are 162. People may also say target account. A prospect is not a customer, because it has never bought anything.
#Prospects and existing customers are available as governed metrics named # of Prospects and # Existing Customers. They total 438, the accounts that have opportunities, not the 500 account base, because 62 accounts have no opportunity records at all. Never say they add up to the full account base.
#The metric named # Existing Customers counts accounts that have bought, which is 276. It is not the full account base. If a user asks how many customers there are without qualifying it, answer 500 and say that is every account, then offer 276 as the number that have bought.
#When prospects or existing customers are filtered by opportunity stage, filtering to an open stage hides every won deal so existing customers falls to zero, and filtering to Closed Won sends prospects to zero. Explain that rather than presenting a zero on its own.
label: SDX Opportunity2

semanticCalculatedDimensions.description: Shows if an account has ever had a closed won opportunity by close date, returning true for all future close dates once one is found. Uses Account and Opportunity tables.
semanticCalculatedDimensions.label: Account Has Closed Won Opportunity Flag Final

semanticCalculatedDimensions.description: True when the opportunity's close date has moved at least once. Use to isolate deals with forecast instability; Close Date Change Count gives the number of moves.
semanticCalculatedDimensions.expression: IF [Opportunity].[CloseDateChangeCount] > 0 then true ELSE false END
semanticCalculatedDimensions.label: Close Date Moved

semanticCalculatedDimensions.description: True when the product is not limited to ICE, meaning powertrain compatibility is Hybrid-Compatible or Both. Use for ICE-to-hybrid transition and product mix analysis.
semanticCalculatedDimensions.expression: IF [Product].[PowertrainCompatibility] = "ICE" then false ELSE true END
semanticCalculatedDimensions.label: Hybrid-Compatible Product

semanticCalculatedDimensions.description: Shows the earliest close date among closed won opportunities for each account, regardless of the view's filters or dimensions. Uses Account and Opportunity tables, grouped by account.
semanticCalculatedDimensions.label: Min Close Date Per Account

semanticCalculatedDimensions.description: True when the opportunity is still open, i.e. not Closed Won or Closed Lost. 594 of the 1500 deals are open. The inverse of Closed Opportunity. Use to scope pipeline questions.
semanticCalculatedDimensions.expression: IF [Opportunity].[IsClosed] then false ELSE true END
semanticCalculatedDimensions.label: Open Opportunity

semanticCalculatedDimensions.description: Checks if an opportunity is closed by returning its closed status as a true or false value. Uses only the Opportunity table.
semanticCalculatedDimensions.label: Opportunity Closed Status

semanticCalculatedDimensions.description: Labels each account as 'New Customer' if it has no closed won opportunities, otherwise as 'Existing Customer', using data from Account and Opportunity tables to distinguish customer status.
semanticCalculatedDimensions.expression: IF ISNULL([gen_ai_Account_Has_Closed_Won_Opportunity_Flag_clc]) OR NOT [gen_ai_Account_Has_Closed_Won_Opportunity_Flag_clc] THEN "New Customer" ELSE "Existing Customer" END
semanticCalculatedDimensions.label: Customer Status Label

semanticCalculatedDimensions.expression: IF [Account_Has_Closed_Won_clc] = 0 OR ISNULL([Account_Has_Closed_Won_clc]) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
semanticCalculatedDimensions.label: New Customer Helper

semanticCalculatedDimensions.description: Win rate for a product family, returned as text so it can be used as a discrete row header. Fixed to Product Family, so it does not recalculate under any other breakdown. For any other slice use the Win Rate measure instead.
semanticCalculatedDimensions.expression: STR(ROUND(100 * { FIXED [Product].[ProductFamily] : COUNTD(IF [Opportunity].[IsWon] THEN [Opportunity].[OpportunityId] ELSE NULL END) / COUNTD(IF [Opportunity].[IsClosed] THEN [Opportunity].[OpportunityId] ELSE NULL END) }, 1)) + "%"
semanticCalculatedDimensions.label: Win Rate (Discrete)

semanticCalculatedDimensions.description: Creates a three-letter abbreviation for each product family name using a CASE statement. If the product family is not listed, uses the first three uppercase letters of the name. Uses only the Product table.
semanticCalculatedDimensions.expression: CASE [Product].[ProductFamily] WHEN "Hybrid Electric" THEN "HYE" WHEN "Internal Combustion Engine" THEN "ICE" WHEN "Plug-In Hybrid" THEN "PIH" WHEN "Battery Electric" THEN "BAE" WHEN "Fuel Cell" THEN "FCE" ELSE LEFT(UPPER([Product].[ProductFamily]), 3) END
semanticCalculatedDimensions.label: Product Family Abbreviation CASE

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Gross margin as a share of net revenue on Closed Won business only, a decimal where 0.314 means 31.4%. A ratio of summed dollars, never an average of line rates. Company wide value is 0.3144. Use the unscoped Gross Margin Rate for all pursued business.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.expression: SUM(IF [Opportunity].[IsWon] then [OpportunityLineItem].[GrossMarginAmount] ELSE 0 END) / SUM(IF [Opportunity].[IsWon] then [OpportunityLineItem].[NetRevenue] ELSE 0 END)
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Gross Margin Rate (Won)

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Average days from creation to close, for closed opportunities only. Sales cycle is 0 on all 594 open deals, so leaving them in drags the average to 98 instead of the correct 163. Lower is better.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Average Sales Cycle Days

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Total open pipeline value in USD. Sums Opportunity Amount for open deals only and contributes 0 for closed ones, so use it as a total rather than an average.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Open Opportunity Amount

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Average discount across opportunities, as a decimal where 0.077 means 7.7 percent. Each opportunity already carries a revenue weighted discount, so this is a plain average of those values. Do not weight again. Lower is better.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Average Discount Rate

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Net revenue on open opportunities measured at the product line, so it breaks down by product, family, or category without overstating. Totals the same 832.06 million as the Open Pipeline metric. Use Open Pipeline for opportunity level questions.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Open Pipeline at Product Level

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Won business in USD measured at the product line, so it can be broken down by product, product family, or category without overstating. Totals the same 393.87 million as Bookings Amount. Use Bookings Amount for opportunity level questions.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Bookings at Product Level

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Shows if an account has ever had a closed won opportunity, regardless of close date, by account name. Uses Account and Opportunity tables.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Account Has Closed Won Opportunity Flag

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Total won business in USD. Sums Opportunity Amount for Closed Won deals only and contributes 0 otherwise, so use it as a total rather than an average.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Bookings Amount

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Number of opportunities still open, counted distinctly. Company total is 594. Not part of win rate, which uses closed deals only. Use with Open Pipeline for value alongside volume.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.expression: COUNTD(IF NOT [Opportunity].[IsClosed] then [Opportunity].[OpportunityId] ELSE NULL END)
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Open Deal Count

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: 1 when an open opportunity has slipped 90 or more days and is also flagged high risk, otherwise 0. Sum it for a count. High risk means a risk score of 60 or more. Expect 143 of the 252 badly slipped deals.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.expression: IF [Opportunity].[IsClosed] then 0 ELSE IF [AnalyticsGoldOpportunity].[CloseDateSlipDays] >= 90 AND [AnalyticsGoldOpportunity].[HighRiskFlag] then 1 ELSE 0 END END
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Slipped High Risk Opportunities

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Average value in USD of a Closed Won opportunity. Won amount divided by the count of distinct won deals, so open and lost deals affect neither side. Use for program size and seller ramp comparisons.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.expression: SUM(IF [Opportunity].[IsWon] then [Opportunity].[Amount] ELSE 0 END) / COUNTD(IF [Opportunity].[IsWon] then [Opportunity].[OpportunityId] ELSE NULL END)
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Average Deal Size

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Share of closed opportunities that were won, as a decimal where 0.52 means 52 percent. Distinct won deals divided by distinct closed deals, so open deals are excluded from both sides. Great Lakes is 0.671 and Southeast is 0.416.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.expression: COUNTD(IF [Opportunity].[IsWon] then [Opportunity].[OpportunityId] ELSE NULL END) / COUNTD(IF [Opportunity].[IsClosed] then [Opportunity].[OpportunityId] ELSE NULL END)
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Win Rate

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: 1 when an OPEN opportunity's close date has slipped 90 or more days from its original commitment, otherwise 0. Sum it for a count of badly slipped deals. An average divides by all 1500 deals, not just the 594 open ones.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.expression: IF [Opportunity].[IsClosed] then 0 ELSE IF [AnalyticsGoldOpportunity].[CloseDateSlipDays] >= 90 then 1 ELSE 0 END END
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Slipped 90 or More Days

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Number of Closed Won opportunities, counted distinctly so it cannot inflate at line item grain. Company total is 471. Pair with Lost Deal Count for a win to loss ratio, or use Win Rate for the percentage.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Won Deal Count

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Average number of distinct product families on an opportunity. Higher means broader attach across the platform. Use to compare sellers or programs on cross selling breadth.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Product Family Attach Rate

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Share of net revenue from products not limited to ICE, as a decimal where 0.819 means 81.9 percent. Group by opportunity created year, not close date, or the trend flattens. Runs 0.631 in 2023 to 0.819 in 2026.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Hybrid-Compatible Revenue Share

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Distinct accounts with at least one Closed Won opportunity in scope. Returns 276 unfiltered. Counts accounts, not rows, and uses no LOD, so it responds to dashboard filters and cannot inflate to opportunity or line item grain.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Existing Customer Accounts

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Distinct accounts with no Closed Won opportunity. Returns 162. Referencing Opportunity restricts the account total to those appearing in Opportunity, so the 62 accounts with no opportunity records are excluded and this cannot reach the full 500 base.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.expression: COUNTD([Account].[AccountId]) - COUNTD(IF [Opportunity].[IsWon] then [Opportunity].[AccountId2] ELSE NULL END)
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: New Customer Accounts

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Calculates the total value in USD of opportunities that are closed and not won, summing the opportunity amount for these deals only. Use this to measure the total lost opportunity value. Uses only the Opportunity table.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.expression: IF [Opportunity].[IsClosed] AND NOT [Opportunity].[IsWon] then [Opportunity].[Amount] ELSE 0 END
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Lost Opportunity Amount

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Gross margin as a share of net revenue, as a decimal where 0.309 means 30.9 percent. A ratio of summed dollars, not an average of the per line rate, which gives a different and wrong answer. Company wide value is 0.309.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Gross Margin Rate

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Net revenue in USD from products not limited to ICE. Sums line-item net revenue where powertrain compatibility is Hybrid-Compatible or Both, and 0 for ICE-only. Use for ICE-to-hybrid transition analysis.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Hybrid-Compatible Revenue

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Calculates the average net revenue for each country, regardless of the view's current filters or dimensions. Uses Account, OpportunityLineItem, and related tables.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Average Net Revenue Per Country

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Gross margin dollars on Closed Won business measured at the product line, so it decomposes exactly by product or family. Totals 123.85 million USD. An unscoped sum of Gross Margin Amount reaches 484.53 million by including open and lost deals.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Gross Margin at Product Level (Won)

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Number of Closed Lost opportunities, counted distinctly. Company total is 435. Pair with Won Deal Count for a win to loss ratio. Closed deals are 906, so the company win rate is 52 percent.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.expression: COUNTD(IF [Opportunity].[IsClosed] AND NOT [Opportunity].[IsWon] then [Opportunity].[OpportunityId] ELSE NULL END)
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Lost Deal Count

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Counts the number of existing customers by summing accounts labeled as 'Existing Customer', identified by having at least one closed won opportunity in the sales data.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Existing Customers

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Counts the number of accounts classified as 'New Customer', identifying those without any closed won opportunities by analyzing account and opportunity data.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: New Customers

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Calculates the average win rate for each product family by dividing the number of distinct won opportunities by the number of distinct closed opportunities, considering only opportunities that are either won or lost. Excludes deals that are still in
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.expression: COUNTD(IF [Opportunity].[IsWon] THEN [Opportunity].[OpportunityId] ELSE NULL END) / COUNTD(IF [Opportunity].[IsClosed] THEN [Opportunity].[OpportunityId] ELSE NULL END)
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: Win Rate By Product Family

semanticCalculatedMeasurements.description: Value of open opportunities flagged high risk, in USD. Subset of Open Pipeline, at deal grain from Opportunity.Amount. Do not break down by Product: it fans out about 3.4x through line items. Risk flags are a 2026-06-30 snapshot.
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.expression: SUM(IF NOT [Opportunity].[IsClosed] AND [AnalyticsGoldOpportunity].[HighRiskFlag] THEN [Opportunity].[Amount] ELSE 0 END)
semanticCalculatedMeasurements.label: High Risk Pipeline Amount

semanticDataObjects.description: Customer organizations Apex Motion sells to: OEM, Tier 1/2 supplier, distributor, fleet and aftermarket. One row per account (500). Use for customer type, tier, strategic status and default customer geography. Also called customers, clients, accounts.
semanticDataObjects.label: Account

semanticDimensions.description: Unique identifier for a customer organization and the primary key of Accounts, e.g. 001000000000001AAA. Joined from Contacts and Opportunities. Use for distinct customer counts. Also called customer ID, account number.
semanticDimensions.label: Account ID

semanticDimensions.description: Name of the customer organization, e.g. Northstar Automotive Group. The label to show when naming an account. Also called customer name, client name.
semanticDimensions.label: Account Name

semanticDimensions.description: Account lifecycle status. Every account here is Active, so this field cannot separate groups.
semanticDimensions.label: Account Status

semanticDimensions.description: Commercial relationship tier ranking how important the account is. One of Platinum, Gold, Silver, Standard, with Platinum highest.
semanticDimensions.label: Account Tier

semanticDimensions.description: Customer class. One of OEM, Tier 1 Supplier, Tier 2 Supplier, Distributor, Fleet, Aftermarket. Also called customer type, customer class, account class.
semanticDimensions.label: Account Type

semanticDimensions.description: City of the account's primary address, e.g. Grand Rapids. 38 cities across the US, Canada and Mexico.
semanticDimensions.label: City

semanticDimensions.description: Country of the account's primary address. One of USA, Canada, Mexico.
semanticDimensions.label: Country

semanticDimensions.description: Date the customer relationship began, 2008 onward. Use for customer tenure and for new versus long-standing customer analysis.
semanticDimensions.label: Customer Since Date

semanticDimensions.description: Industry classification of the customer. One of Automotive Manufacturing, Automotive Aftermarket, Fleet Operations.
semanticDimensions.label: Industry

semanticDimensions.description: The account's main powertrain buying focus. One of ICE, Hybrid, Both. Use for ICE-to-hybrid transition analysis.
semanticDimensions.label: Primary Powertrain Focus

semanticDimensions.description: Links the account to its customer sales territory. This is the DEFAULT geography path for customer and opportunity analysis; do not substitute the opportunity owner's territory. Also called customer territory, account territory.
semanticDimensions.label: Customer Territory ID

semanticDimensions.description: State or province of the account's primary address, e.g. Michigan. 32 distinct values.
semanticDimensions.label: State or Province

semanticDimensions.description: True/false flag marking accounts with elevated executive visibility. True means a strategic account.
semanticDimensions.label: Strategic Account

semanticMeasurements.description: Approximate annual revenue of the customer organization in USD, from 89M to 37B. A size attribute of the customer, not Apex Motion sales. Sum or average across accounts only, never across opportunities.
semanticMeasurements.label: Annual Revenue

semanticMeasurements.description: Approximate headcount at the customer organization, from 287 to 57,218. A size attribute of the customer. Sum or average across accounts only, never across opportunities.
semanticMeasurements.label: Employee Count

semanticDataObjects.description: Named people at customer accounts across engineering, procurement, finance, operations and leadership. One row per contact (900), each tied to one account. Use only when contact-level detail or decision-role analysis is asked for.
semanticDataObjects.label: Contact

semanticDimensions.description: Links the contact to the customer account they work for. Join to Accounts for customer type, tier and territory.
semanticDimensions.label: Account ID

semanticDimensions.description: True/false flag for whether the contact is still active at the account.
semanticDimensions.label: Active Contact

semanticDimensions.description: Unique identifier for a person at a customer account and the primary key of Account Contacts.
semanticDimensions.label: Contact ID

semanticDimensions.description: Date the contact record was created, 2018 onward. Default date field for Account Contacts.
semanticDimensions.label: Created Date

semanticDimensions.description: The contact's role in a buying decision. One of Decision Maker, Economic Buyer, Executive Sponsor, Influencer, Technical Buyer.
semanticDimensions.label: Decision Role

semanticDimensions.description: Contact's functional department. One of Engineering, Procurement, Operations, Quality, Finance, Program Management, Leadership.
semanticDimensions.label: Department

semanticDimensions.description: Synthetic email address that is not deliverable. Do not use for outreach.
semanticDimensions.label: Email

semanticDimensions.description: Contact's given name. Use Contact Name when you need the full name.
semanticDimensions.label: First Name

semanticDimensions.description: Contact's full name, e.g. Nadia Lee. The label to show when naming a contact.
semanticDimensions.label: Contact Name

semanticDimensions.description: Contact's job title at the customer. One of 8 values including Plant Manager, Chief Engineer, Director of Procurement, Senior Buyer and VP of Operations.
semanticDimensions.label: Job Title

semanticDimensions.description: Contact's family name. Use Contact Name when you need the full name.
semanticDimensions.label: Last Name

semanticDimensions.description: Synthetic telephone number that is not a real line. Do not use for outreach.
semanticDimensions.label: Phone

semanticDataObjects.description: Apex Motion sales staff and the sales hierarchy: VP Sales, Sales Directors, Regional Managers and Account Executives. One row per person (30). Owns opportunities. Also called sellers, sales reps, account executives, salespeople.
semanticDataObjects.label: User

semanticDimensions.description: True/false flag for an active seller. All 30 are active, so this field cannot separate groups.
semanticDimensions.label: Active Team Member

semanticDimensions.description: Sales director organization the member rolls up to. One of Central Sales, Eastern Sales, Western and International Sales, Executive Sales. Use this for hierarchy rollups.
semanticDimensions.label: Director Group

semanticDimensions.description: Sales team member's name, e.g. Cameron Brooks. The label to show when naming a seller. Also called salesperson, seller, sales rep, account executive.
semanticDimensions.label: Sales Team Member Name

semanticDimensions.description: Date the sales team member was hired. Default date field for Sales Team Members. Use for tenure analysis.
semanticDimensions.label: Hire Date

semanticDimensions.description: Links the team member to their home Apex Motion office or plant. Use for home office and operating footprint analysis.
semanticDimensions.label: Home Location ID

semanticDimensions.description: The team member's manager, pointing at another sales team member. Only the VP Sales record has no manager. Not joined in this model, so manager attributes cannot be reached through it.
semanticDimensions.label: Manager User ID

semanticDimensions.description: Start of a documented new-hire ramp period. Populated for one seller only (2025-04-01) and empty for the other 29. Use for new account executive productivity analysis.
semanticDimensions.label: Ramp Start Date

semanticDimensions.description: Level in the sales hierarchy. One of VP Sales, Sales Director, Regional Manager, Account Executive. Filter to Account Executive for individual seller analysis. Also called sales role, hierarchy level.
semanticDimensions.label: Role Level

semanticDimensions.description: The seller's own assigned territory, empty for the 5 leaders above regional level. Use ONLY for explicitly seller-focused geography; the default path is the account's territory. Not joined in this model.
semanticDimensions.label: Owner Territory ID

semanticDimensions.description: Specific job title in the sales organization, e.g. Regional Manager, Great Lakes. 12 values, more granular than Role Level.
semanticDimensions.label: Title

semanticDimensions.description: Unique identifier for a sales team member and the primary key of Sales Team Members. Joined from the opportunity owner. Also called seller ID, rep ID.
semanticDimensions.label: User ID

semanticDataObjects.description: Apex Motion's automotive component catalog: family, category, powertrain compatibility, list price, standard cost and plant. One row per component (75). Use for product mix, attach, margin, substitution and ICE-to-hybrid analysis. Also called parts.
semanticDataObjects.label: Product

semanticDimensions.description: True/false flag for an active catalog product. All 75 are active, so this field cannot separate groups.
semanticDimensions.label: Active Product

semanticDimensions.description: Date the product was discontinued. Empty for all 75 products, since none have been discontinued.
semanticDimensions.label: Discontinue Date

semanticDimensions.description: Date the product launched, 2017 onward. Default date field for Products.
semanticDimensions.label: Launch Date

semanticDimensions.description: Which powertrains the component fits. One of ICE, Hybrid-Compatible, Both. Anything other than ICE counts as hybrid-capable. Also called powertrain fit.
semanticDimensions.label: Powertrain Compatibility

semanticDimensions.description: City of the plant that makes the component. One of Fort Wayne, Columbus, Bowling Green.
semanticDimensions.label: Primary Plant City

semanticDimensions.description: Links the product to the plant that makes it. Not joined in this model; use Primary Plant City to analyse by plant.
semanticDimensions.label: Primary Plant Location ID

semanticDimensions.description: Component category within a family, e.g. Piston Set. 48 values, more granular than Product Family.
semanticDimensions.label: Product Category

semanticDimensions.description: Portable part code for the component, e.g. AMC-0001. An alternate identifier used outside this system. Also called part number, SKU.
semanticDimensions.label: Product Code

semanticDimensions.description: Component family, one of six: Engine Components, Thermal Management, Fuel and Fluid Systems, Ignition and Electronics, Emissions and Air Management, Hybrid and Electrification Support. Also called component family.
semanticDimensions.label: Product Family

semanticDimensions.description: Unique identifier for an automotive component and the primary key of Products. Joined from Opportunity Products.
semanticDimensions.label: Product ID

semanticDimensions.description: Component name, e.g. Piston Set A01. The label to show when naming a product.
semanticDimensions.label: Product Name

semanticMeasurements.description: Catalog list price per unit in USD, 70 to 603. A catalog attribute, so average across products. For quoted prices use Opportunity Products instead.
semanticMeasurements.label: List Price

semanticMeasurements.description: Catalog margin rate as a decimal fraction, 0.27 to 0.45, where 0.3712 means 37.12%. Average across products. For realized margin use the governed Gross Margin Rate metric.
semanticMeasurements.label: Standard Gross Margin Rate

semanticMeasurements.description: Catalog standard cost per unit in USD, 51 to 412. A catalog attribute, so average across products. For quoted cost use Opportunity Products instead.
semanticMeasurements.label: Standard Unit Cost

semanticDataObjects.description: Sales pursuits for customer vehicle programs, holding pipeline, outcome, owner, forecast, activity and close-date context. One row per opportunity (1500). The primary sales analysis grain. Also called deals, pursuits, RFQs, quotes.
semanticDataObjects.label: Opportunity

semanticDimensions.description: Links the pursuit to its customer account. Join to Accounts for customer type, tier and the default sales territory.
semanticDimensions.label: Account ID

semanticDimensions.description: Expected close date while open and actual close date once closed. Default date field for Opportunities. Be lifecycle aware: forecast timing for open deals, sales cycle for closed ones.
semanticDimensions.label: Close Date

semanticDimensions.description: Date the pursuit was created. Use as the pipeline creation date for cohort and ageing analysis.
semanticDimensions.label: Created Date

semanticDimensions.description: Currency of the amounts. Every row is USD, so this field cannot separate groups.
semanticDimensions.label: Currency ISO Code

semanticDimensions.description: The customer's underlying business need. One of Platform Launch, Cost Reduction, Capacity Expansion, Hybrid Readiness, Quality Improvement, Supplier Consolidation.
semanticDimensions.label: Customer Need

semanticDimensions.description: Forecast rollup bucket. One of Pipeline, Best Case, Commit, Closed.
semanticDimensions.label: Forecast Category

semanticDimensions.description: True/false flag, true only for Closed Won and Closed Lost. 906 of the 1500 deals are closed and 594 are open pipeline.
semanticDimensions.label: Closed

semanticDimensions.description: True/false flag, true only for Closed Won. Combine with Closed Opportunity to compute win rate.
semanticDimensions.label: Won

semanticDimensions.description: Date of the most recent sales activity on the deal. Use for pipeline freshness and stale deal analysis.
semanticDimensions.label: Last Activity Date

semanticDimensions.description: How the pursuit originated. One of Existing Relationship, RFQ, Referral, Inbound, Partner, Trade Event.
semanticDimensions.label: Lead Source

semanticDimensions.description: Why a deal was lost. One of Price, Competitor, Technical Fit, Timing, No Decision, Program Cancelled. Populated only for the 435 Closed Lost deals.
semanticDimensions.label: Loss Reason

semanticDimensions.description: The seller's next planned action on an open deal, one of 5 standard actions. Empty for the 906 closed deals.
semanticDimensions.label: Next Step

semanticDimensions.description: Unique identifier for a sales pursuit and the primary key of Opportunities. Joined from Opportunity Products and Analytics Gold. Use for distinct deal counts. Also called deal ID, pursuit ID.
semanticDimensions.label: Opportunity ID

semanticDimensions.description: Name of the pursuit, combining customer, vehicle program and sequence number. The label to show when naming a deal. Also called deal, sales opportunity, pursuit, RFQ, quote.
semanticDimensions.label: Opportunity Name

semanticDimensions.description: Nature of the pursuit. One of New Program, Expansion, Replacement, Requote.
semanticDimensions.label: Opportunity Type

semanticDimensions.description: The first close date ever committed for this deal. Compare with Close Date to measure forecast slippage. Also called initial close date.
semanticDimensions.label: Original Close Date

semanticDimensions.description: Links the pursuit to the seller who owns it. 20 of the 30 team members own deals. Also called opportunity owner, seller, sales rep.
semanticDimensions.label: Owner User ID

semanticDimensions.description: Powertrain context of the pursuit, either ICE or Hybrid. Use for ICE-to-hybrid transition analysis.
semanticDimensions.label: Powertrain Type

semanticDimensions.description: The close date immediately before the most recent change. Empty for the 1,240 deals whose close date never moved.
semanticDimensions.label: Prior Close Date

semanticDimensions.description: Current stage if open, final stage if closed. One of Prospecting, Qualification, Technical Review, Proposal or Quote, Negotiation, Closed Won, Closed Lost.
semanticDimensions.label: Stage Name

semanticDimensions.description: Customer vehicle or commercial program the pursuit supplies, e.g. Northstar Nova Compact Crossover. 659 distinct programs.
semanticDimensions.label: Vehicle Program Name

semanticDimensions.description: Target vehicle or channel segment. One of Compact Crossover, Urban Commuter, Mid-Size Sedan, Light Truck, Fleet Van, Aftermarket Program.
semanticDimensions.label: Vehicle Segment

semanticMeasurements.description: Value of the pursuit in USD, 64K to 6.6M, equal to its summed line-item net revenue. Pipeline means open deals, bookings means Closed Won. Also called opportunity value, deal value, deal size.
semanticMeasurements.label: Amount

semanticMeasurements.description: Number of times the close date moved, 0 to 5. Sum across deals. Higher counts signal forecast instability.
semanticMeasurements.label: Close Date Change Count

semanticMeasurements.description: Win probability aligned to stage, stored as a decimal fraction from 0.0 to 1.0 where 0.6 means 60%. Multiply by Amount to weight the pipeline. Do NOT divide by 100.
semanticMeasurements.label: Probability

semanticDataObjects.description: Products quoted on an opportunity with quantity, price, discount, net revenue, cost and gross margin. One row per product per opportunity (4500). Aggregate to opportunity level before combining with opportunity-grain measures.
semanticDataObjects.label: Opportunity Line Item

semanticDimensions.description: Currency of the line amounts. Every row is USD, so this field cannot separate groups.
semanticDimensions.label: Currency ISO Code

semanticDimensions.description: Links the line to its parent opportunity. Aggregate line measures to this key before combining them with opportunity-grain measures.
semanticDimensions.label: Opportunity ID

semanticDimensions.description: Unique identifier for one product line on one opportunity and the primary key of Opportunity Products.
semanticDimensions.label: Opportunity Line Item ID

semanticDimensions.description: Links the line to the product catalog. Join to Products for family, category and powertrain compatibility.
semanticDimensions.label: Product ID

semanticDimensions.description: True/false flag marking a line where a lower-cost product was substituted. Use for substitution and price pressure analysis.
semanticDimensions.label: Product Substitution

semanticMeasurements.description: Discount on this line as a decimal fraction, 0.0 to 0.26, where 0.0299 means 2.99%. Do NOT average across rows; use the revenue-weighted Average Discount. Also called discount, realized discount rate.
semanticMeasurements.label: Discount Rate

semanticMeasurements.description: Quantity times unit cost in USD, so the total cost of the line. Sum across lines.
semanticMeasurements.label: Extended Cost

semanticMeasurements.description: Net revenue less extended cost, in USD. Sum across lines. Also called gross margin, gross profit.
semanticMeasurements.label: Gross Margin Amount

semanticMeasurements.description: Line gross margin divided by line net revenue, a decimal fraction 0.05 to 0.46. Do NOT average across rows; divide total gross margin by total net revenue.
semanticMeasurements.label: Gross Margin Rate

semanticMeasurements.description: Quantity times list unit price in USD, so revenue before any discount. Sum across lines.
semanticMeasurements.label: List Revenue

semanticMeasurements.description: Quoted list price per unit in USD before discount, 66 to 639. Average across lines.
semanticMeasurements.label: List Unit Price

semanticMeasurements.description: Value of one product line in USD, quantity times net unit price, regardless of outcome. Sums to Opportunity Value. Not revenue. Use Bookings at Product Level for won business broken down by product.
semanticMeasurements.label: Line Opportunity Value

semanticMeasurements.description: Price per unit in USD after discount, 56 to 616. List Unit Price less the discount.
semanticMeasurements.label: Net Unit Price

semanticMeasurements.description: Units of the product quoted on this line, 46 to 46,059. Sum across lines.
semanticMeasurements.label: Quantity

semanticMeasurements.description: Cost per unit in USD for this quoted line, 50 to 412.
semanticMeasurements.label: Unit Cost

semanticDataObjects.description: Apex Motion's own facilities: headquarters, manufacturing plants, engineering centers, distribution and sales offices. One row per location (8). Use for seller home office, plant and operating footprint. These are not customer addresses.
semanticDataObjects.label: Company Location

semanticDimensions.description: City of the Apex Motion facility. One of Detroit, Fort Wayne, Columbus, Bowling Green, Dallas, Charlotte, Windsor, Monterrey.
semanticDimensions.label: Facility City

semanticDimensions.description: Country of the Apex Motion facility. One of USA, Canada, Mexico.
semanticDimensions.label: Facility Country

semanticDimensions.description: Unique identifier for an Apex Motion facility and the primary key of Company Locations, e.g. Location001.
semanticDimensions.label: Location ID

semanticDimensions.description: Name of the Apex Motion facility, e.g. Apex Motion Headquarters. The label to show when naming a location.
semanticDimensions.label: Location Name

semanticDimensions.description: Kind of facility. One of Headquarters, Manufacturing Plant, Engineering Center, Distribution Center, Sales Office, Sales and Engineering Office.
semanticDimensions.label: Location Type

semanticDimensions.description: What the facility mainly does, e.g. Executive leadership and sales operations. One distinct role per location.
semanticDimensions.label: Primary Role

semanticDimensions.description: The business region this facility belongs to. Not joined in this model; use Region Name on this table to group locations by region.
semanticDimensions.label: Facility Region ID

semanticDimensions.description: Business region of the facility, e.g. Great Lakes. Only 5 of the 7 regions appear here, since Northeast and West have no facility.
semanticDimensions.label: Facility Region

semanticDimensions.description: State or province of the Apex Motion facility, e.g. Michigan. 8 values, one per location.
semanticDimensions.label: Facility State or Province

semanticDataObjects.description: Customer sales territories defining customer geography, state coverage, director group and anchor office. One row per territory (7). Default geography path is account to territory; use owner territory only for explicit seller questions.
semanticDataObjects.label: Sales Territory

semanticDimensions.description: The states or provinces the territory covers, e.g. MI, OH, IN, IL, WI. Free text, one per territory.
semanticDimensions.label: Coverage Summary

semanticDimensions.description: Sales director organization covering the territory. One of Central Sales, Eastern Sales, Western and International Sales.
semanticDimensions.label: Territory Director Group

semanticDimensions.description: The Apex Motion facility that anchors the territory. Not joined in this model; 5 of the 8 locations serve as anchors.
semanticDimensions.label: Primary Location ID

semanticDimensions.description: Links the territory to its parent business region. Use this path to roll territories up to regions.
semanticDimensions.label: Territory Region ID

semanticDimensions.description: Parent business region name, denormalized here so you can group by region without a join.
semanticDimensions.label: Territory Region

semanticDimensions.description: Unique identifier for a customer sales territory and the primary key of Sales Territories, e.g. TerritoryGL. Joined from the account's territory.
semanticDimensions.label: Territory ID

semanticDimensions.description: Name of the customer sales territory. One of Great Lakes, Northeast, Southeast, South Central, West, Canada, Mexico.
semanticDimensions.label: Territory Name

semanticDataObjects.description: Parent business regions grouping sales territories and company locations, with country scope, director ownership and display order. One row per region (7). Use for executive geographic rollups. Also called regions.
semanticDataObjects.label: Business Region

semanticDimensions.description: Main country the region covers. One of USA, Canada, Mexico.
semanticDimensions.label: Country Scope

semanticDimensions.description: Short business context for the region, e.g. Mature Midwest automotive customer base. Free text, one per region.
semanticDimensions.label: Description

semanticDimensions.description: Sales director organization that owns the region. One of Central Sales, Eastern Sales, Western and International Sales.
semanticDimensions.label: Region Director Group

semanticDimensions.description: Unique identifier for a business region and the primary key of Business Regions, e.g. RegionGL. Joined from Sales Territories.
semanticDimensions.label: Sales Region ID

semanticDimensions.description: Name of the business region. One of Great Lakes, Northeast, Southeast, South Central, West, Canada, Mexico. The label to show when naming a region.
semanticDimensions.label: Sales Region

semanticMeasurements.description: Preferred display order for regions, 1 through 7. A sequencing attribute rather than a measure, so do not sum or average it.
semanticMeasurements.label: Sort Order

semanticDataObjects.description: Certified opportunity-level analytics precomputed as of 2026-06-30: age, cycle time, product attach, margin, slippage, mix, health, risk and confidence. One row per opportunity (1500). Join 1:1 to Opportunities; do not rebuild as calculations.
semanticDataObjects.label: Analytics Gold Opportunity

semanticDimensions.description: The fixed analysis date for every row, always 2026-06-30. Open-deal measures are computed as of this date, which is what makes them reproducible.
semanticDimensions.label: As Of Date

semanticDimensions.description: True/false flag, true when an open deal's risk score reaches 60. Use to size at-risk pipeline.
semanticDimensions.label: High Risk

semanticDimensions.description: Pre-banded age group for the deal. One of 0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-180, 181-365, 365+. Use this rather than bucketing Opportunity Age yourself.
semanticDimensions.label: Opportunity Age Bucket

semanticDimensions.description: The opportunity this gold row describes and the primary key of Analytics Gold. Exactly one gold row per opportunity, so the join to Opportunities is one to one.
semanticDimensions.label: Opportunity ID

semanticDimensions.description: True/false flag, true when an open deal covers one or fewer product families, marking a cross-sell or attach opening.
semanticDimensions.label: Product Attach Opportunity

semanticMeasurements.description: Revenue-weighted discount rate for the whole deal, a decimal fraction 0.0005 to 0.2463 where 0.06 means 6%. Already weighted correctly, so use this rather than averaging line discounts.
semanticMeasurements.label: Average Discount

semanticMeasurements.description: Number of times the deal's close date moved, 0 to 5. Sum across deals. Higher counts signal forecast instability.
semanticMeasurements.label: Close Date Change Count

semanticMeasurements.description: Days the close date slipped beyond the original commitment, 0 to 1,268 and never negative. 0 means no slip. Average across deals. Also called slip days, close date movement.
semanticMeasurements.label: Close Date Slip Days

semanticMeasurements.description: Composite confidence score for OPEN deals from probability, forecast category and slippage. Observed 11 to 89 and higher is better. Empty for the 906 closed deals. Also called confidence score.
semanticMeasurements.label: Forecast Confidence

semanticMeasurements.description: Summed line-item gross margin for the deal in USD, 17K to 2.3M. Use at deal level to avoid line-item fan-out. Also called gross margin, gross profit.
semanticMeasurements.label: Opportunity Gross Margin

semanticMeasurements.description: Deal gross margin divided by deal net revenue, a decimal fraction 0.12 to 0.44 where 0.276 means 27.6%. Already a correct ratio of sums at deal level.
semanticMeasurements.label: Opportunity Gross Margin Rate

semanticMeasurements.description: Share of the deal's net revenue from products not limited to ICE, a decimal fraction 0.0 to 1.0 where 0.48 means 48%. Use for ICE-to-hybrid transition analysis.
semanticMeasurements.label: Hybrid Product Share

semanticMeasurements.description: Total value of the opportunity in USD regardless of outcome, so it includes won, lost and still open deals. Not revenue and not performance. Matches Opportunity Amount. Use Bookings Amount for won business.
semanticMeasurements.label: Opportunity Value

semanticMeasurements.description: Days the deal has existed: created to close for closed deals, created to 2026-06-30 for open ones. 16 to 1,272 days. Average across deals. Also called days open, deal age, time open.
semanticMeasurements.label: Opportunity Age

semanticMeasurements.description: Composite health score for OPEN deals from probability, freshness, margin, slippage and attach breadth. Observed 22 to 87 and higher is better. Empty for the 906 closed deals.
semanticMeasurements.label: Opportunity Health Score

semanticMeasurements.description: Composite risk score for OPEN deals from age, slippage, discount, margin and probability. Observed 4 to 74. LOWER is better and 60 or more counts as high risk. Empty for closed deals.
semanticMeasurements.label: Opportunity Risk Score

semanticMeasurements.description: Days from creation to close, for CLOSED deals only, 45 to 389. Empty for the 594 open deals. Average across closed deals.
semanticMeasurements.label: Sales Cycle Days

semanticMeasurements.description: Distinct products quoted on the deal, 1 to 5. Average across deals.
semanticMeasurements.label: Unique Product Count

semanticMeasurements.description: Distinct product families quoted on the deal, 1 to 5. A value of 1 marks a cross-sell opening. Average across deals.
semanticMeasurements.label: Unique Product Family Count

semanticMeasurements.description: Opportunity amount times win probability, in USD. Populated for the 594 OPEN deals only. The weighted pipeline measure. Sum across deals.
semanticMeasurements.label: Weighted Amount

semanticMetrics.description: Total value of Closed Won opportunities in USD. This is won business, not accounting revenue. Sliceable by region, territory, owner, account, customer type, product family, and state or province.
semanticMetrics.label: Bookings

semanticMetrics.description: Accounts with at least one Closed Won opportunity, so they have bought at least once. Returns 276 of the 500 account base. With Prospects at 162 this totals 438, the accounts that have opportunities, not the full base, because 62 accounts have none.
semanticMetrics.label: # Existing Customers

semanticMetrics.description: Value in USD of opportunities that closed without being won. Not revenue and not pipeline. Pair with Bookings for a value based win rate: Bookings divided by Bookings plus Lost Value is 53.4 percent. Company total is 343.3 million.
semanticMetrics.label: Lost Value

semanticMetrics.description: Accounts with at least one opportunity and no Closed Won deal, so they have never bought. Returns 162. Excludes 62 accounts that have no opportunity records at all, so Prospects plus Customers totals 438, not the 500 account base.
semanticMetrics.label: # of Prospects

semanticMetrics.description: Total value of opportunities that are still open, in USD. Not won business and not revenue. Compare against Bookings for won deals.
semanticMetrics.label: Open Pipeline

semanticMetrics.description: Open pipeline value on deals flagged high risk. Subset of Open Pipeline. No Product breakdowns: they fan out about 3.4x through line items.
semanticMetrics.label: High Risk Pipeline
